data.text: Sourcing starts long before the box arrives

Every figure in the Brickverse catalog goes through the same three checks: sculpt accuracy against the official reference art, paint-line consistency, and joint durability after a hundred pose cycles.

Our team works directly with licensed importers rather than grey-market resellers, which is slower and pricier but means what you see in photos is exactly what ships.

data.caption: First-pass quality check on a new shipment.

data.text: Once a batch clears inspection, it moves to our Melbourne warehouse for the final photography pass you see on every product page.
If it wouldn't pass our own shelf test, it doesn't go up for sale.
data.author: Brickverse QA Team

data.text: Shop anime figures
Plan the shape before you buy pieces

The single biggest mistake first-time builders make is buying bricks before sketching the build. Spend ten minutes with graph paper first — it saves you from ending up with forty of one colour and none of another.

Start small: a single-storey house, a simple vehicle, or a two-colour tower is enough to learn how our building sets snap together before you commit to a 1,000-piece kit.
Sort before you build
Tip most beginners skip: sort loose bricks by colour first, not by shape. It cuts build time roughly in half once a set gets past 200 pieces.

Start screen-free, graduate to code

The kits that stick around longest in a kid's room aren't the flashiest ones — they're the ones with a clear next step. Start with a screen-free logic toy, move to block coding, and only then introduce a text-based language like Python.

Below are five kits from our Coding & STEM range, ordered roughly by age and difficulty.

data.text: Robo Coder and Pixel Bot are our two best beginner sellers, while Drone Builder is aimed squarely at kids already comfortable with block coding and ready for real Python.

Starting small, on purpose
Rather than launch with fifty figures at once, we picked five fan favourites to gauge demand before committing to a full line. All five sold through their first batch in the first week.
Based on how quickly this corner sold through, we're expanding to a full 20-figure lineup next quarter — sign up to our newsletter to get first access.

The most-requested restock of the year
Doraemon has been out of stock since our first shipment sold through in under a week. This restock triples our previous order size, plus adds two characters we've never carried before.
Shop cartoon toys
One shelf, two universes

The brick-built crossover line started as an experiment — would collectors want Marvel and anime characters displayed side by side, built from the same compatible brick system? The answer, from our sales numbers, is a clear yes.
Every figure in this line uses the same base plate size, so they all click together on one display shelf regardless of universe.
